Title: Diagnosis of test `testReflectionObjectCycle`

Details:
The test case `testReflectionObjectCycle` sets up two objects that reference each other, creating a cyclic object graph. When invoking `hashCode()` on one of these objects, the process uses reflection-based hash code generation through the `HashCodeBuilder.reflectionHashCode` method.

The root cause of the stack overflow error is that the reflection-based code traverses the object fields recursively, potentially cycling indefinitely through the cyclic references. To prevent this, the `HashCodeBuilder` maintains a per-thread registry of visited objects to avoid revisiting and endlessly recursing on the same objects.

From the snippet of `reflectionAppend(Object, Class<?>, HashCodeBuilder, boolean, String[])`, it is clear that before processing an object's fields, the method checks if the object is already registered (visited) using `isRegistered(Object)`. If so, it returns immediately to prevent infinite recursion. It registers the object by adding an `IDKey` to a thread-local `Set` (the registry) via `register(Object)` and finally unregisters it after processing.

The failing test indicates the stack overflow happens due to recursion while processing cyclic references, implying that either an object is not correctly registered during the reflective traversal or that the registration check fails. The `getRegistry()` method returns a thread-local set that tracks traversed objects by wrapping them in `IDKey`. If this registry isn't correctly managed or queried, cyclic detection would fail, causing infinite recursion.

Hence, the likely issue is in the logic around the registry's maintenance (registering/unregistering) or equality/hash methods in `IDKey` which cause objects not to be identified as already visited during recursion, leading to stack overflow.

Suggested places to fix:
org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.HashCodeBuilder.reflectionAppend(Object, Class<?>, HashCodeBuilder, boolean, String[])
org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.HashCodeBuilder.isRegistered(Object)
org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.HashCodeBuilder.register(Object)
org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.HashCodeBuilder.unregister(Object)
